sections.h2: Who handles a Gallatin County tax bill
sections.html:
Three Warsaw offices come into play when a house changes hands. The PVA places the value, the Sheriff's Office takes the money, and the County Clerk files deeds and takes assessment appeals.

  • PVA: 200 Washington Street (mail to PO Box 470), Warsaw, KY 41095, phone (859) 567-5621.
  • Sheriff: 106 North Main (mail to PO Box 1025), Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5751. The county's sheriff page links to a tax bill lookup.
  • County Clerk: 803 East Main Street, Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5411, open weekdays until 4:30 in the afternoon.

The City of Warsaw runs its own online payment page for water, sewer and property tax bills, so a house inside the city limits may owe the city as well as the county. Ask both the sheriff and the city which bills attach to an address before you set a closing date, and keep copies of every paid receipt for the buyer's title company. A clean paper trail shortens the closing, because the title search will list any unpaid balance as an exception.

sections.h2: Gallatin County housing and the local market
sections.html:
Gallatin County is small, about 105 square miles, and sits on the Ohio River across from Indiana as part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area. Warsaw is the seat, with Sparta and Glencoe the other communities. Interstate 71 runs through with three exits around Sparta and Glencoe, joined by US 42 and US 127, and the commute averages 29.5 minutes. Most buyers here work somewhere else and live in the county for the room and the price.

The 2020 census found 3,685 housing units with 13.1 percent unoccupied, so a share of the stock is seasonal, vacant or waiting for a buyer. Growth has been slow but steady.

Bills are payable to the sheriff, and the state's collection rules in KRS 134.015 give every owner the same ladder. A 2 percent reduction applies to a bill paid in full by November 1, the printed amount runs through December 31, and late payers owe 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward.

If bill mailing slips, the Department of Revenue can replace the usual dates with a compressed schedule of one month at a discount, one month at face and one month at 5 percent, so read the dates printed on the bill itself. When a house sells, tell the sheriff the new owner's name so later bills reach the right person.

Start at 200 Washington Street. The state requires a PVA conference before any appeal, and visits are easiest right after assessment notices arrive. The tax roll then opens to public view for 13 days in early May.

Once you have met the PVA or a deputy, the County Clerk's office takes your written appeal, which is due by the end of the next business day after viewing closes. The local board of assessment appeals sits about four to five weeks later, for up to five days.

  • Bring facts about the land and buildings, construction costs, insurance details and sale listings of similar properties.
  • Expect to explain your evidence in person with the PVA also present.
  • The board must put the reason for any raise or cut in writing, and you are allowed to record the hearing.

An owner who files but does not attend the hearing cannot continue to the Kentucky Claims Commission, so mark the hearing date on a calendar the day it is set.

For seniors and totally disabled owners, $49,100 is deducted from assessed value in 2025 and 2026. File with the Gallatin County PVA. Because the typical home here is valued at $178,200, the deduction takes a meaningful bite out of the taxable amount.

Disability filers need payments from a federal or retirement-system program covering the whole assessment period, and they renew every year. Owners with a service-connected military disability and people ruled totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems are exempt from that yearly renewal.

If you sell, tell the PVA so the exemption is removed from your name. The buyer can apply for their own if they qualify.

The balance stays with the property. KRS 134.015 calls the tax a personal debt as of the assessment date, and a delinquency lien under KRS 134.420 continues no matter who takes title.

On April 15 the sheriff transfers open bills to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency. Within 30 days the county attorney mails a first notice, a second follows within 60 days, and the clerk's tax sale takes place 90 to 135 days after the transfer. A third-party buyer at that sale can pile on substantial fees.

  1. Ask the sheriff at (859) 567-5751 for a payoff before you list.
  2. If the house is in Warsaw, ask the city whether a water, sewer or city tax bill is open too.
  3. Give the payoff figure to the title company so the balance is cleared from the sale proceeds.
  4. Keep the paid receipts. The title search lists any unpaid balance as an exception to clean title.

A buyer paying cash for the house as-is can close without waiting on a lender and can take the house with the tax balance settled at the table, which suits an owner who has repairs and back taxes stacking up together.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Gallatin County property tax payment?
faqs.a: Send it to the Gallatin County Sheriff, 106 North Main in Warsaw, or PO Box 1025, Warsaw, KY 41095. The county's sheriff page links a tax bill lookup.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Gallatin County PVA?
faqs.a: Call (859) 567-5621 or visit 200 Washington Street in Warsaw. The PVA handles value questions, exemption forms and owner records.

faqs.q: When is the early-payment date in Gallatin County?
faqs.a: It follows the statewide date of November 1, when full payment earns 2 percent off. The face amount is owed through December 31.

faqs.q: Does the City of Warsaw send its own tax bill?
faqs.a: Warsaw offers an online page for water, sewer and property tax bills. Owners inside the city should ask the city and the sheriff which bills apply to their address.

faqs.q: Does a tax lien survive a sale in Gallatin County?
faqs.a: Yes. A delinquency lien stays on the property after a sale until the tax is paid or the period in KRS 134.420 runs out, so settle the balance at closing.
